newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WALLOON GOVT TURNS DOWN BID FOR MORE CLABECQ AID.
newsitem.headline: WALLOON GOVT TURNS DOWN BID FOR MORE CLABECQ AID.

text.p: The Walloon Region turned down a request for more financing from bankrupt steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA on Thursday, casting new doubt on efforts to keep the maker of heavy plate running.

The 800 million Belgian franc request was made by Clabecq's court appointed receivers, who said on Wednesday they would re-employ Clabecq's entire workforce for a limited time if the Walloon Region would cover the extra losses this would create.
But in a statement, the Walloon government -- Clabecq's biggest shareholder and creditor -- said it would cover just 150 million francs of losses, effectively turning down the demand.
The ball now falls back into the court of Clabecq's main union, which represents most of the 1,800 workers who lost their jobs when the company was declared bankrupt on January 3.
The union has so far refused point blank to accept an offer from the receivers to re-employ a limited number of staff while outstanding orders are fulfilled and they search for a buyer.
Even if the unions now change their position the future for Clabecq, which is said to have at least three months work still on its books, remains bleak.
Belgian newspaper Le Soir reported on Thursday it had been told by steelmakers in Britain, France, Germany and the Netherlands that none was interested in buying the company.
